title: Jesse Eisenberg TV Series Produced by Peter Rice Pulled by A24, Deadline Reports
body:
Jesse Eisenberg is set to expand his creative repertoire beyond the silver screen with a new television series for A24, a project that will also be shepherded by veteran producer Peter Rice. The actor‑turned‑writer‑director will not only pen the scripts but also serve as executive producer and director, centering the narrative on a young woman whose story promises the off‑beat, character‑driven sensibility that has become A24’s hallmark. The collaboration marks Eisenberg’s first foray into serialized storytelling and signals a continued partnership with the indie powerhouse that recently released his feature‑directorial debut, *The Debut*, starring Julianne Moore.

Eisenberg’s move into television arrives at a moment when the lines between film and TV are increasingly blurred. Over the past decade, a wave of high‑profile filmmakers—Denis Villeneuve, Greta Gerwig, and Barry Jenkins, among others—have embraced the small‑screen format to explore longer‑form narratives. For Eisenberg, whose career has oscillated between mainstream blockbusters (*The Social Network*, *Batman v Superman*) and indie darlings (*Now You See Me*, *Adventureland*), the shift feels like a natural evolution. The actor’s recent directorial effort, *The Debut*, demonstrated his capacity to blend humor, melancholy, and social commentary, qualities that A24 is likely to amplify in a series format.

Peter Rice’s involvement adds a layer of credibility and strategic alignment. As a long‑time A24 executive producer, Rice has overseen a slate of critically acclaimed series such as *Euphoria* and *The White Lotus*, both of which have redefined television’s aesthetic boundaries. His partnership with Eisenberg suggests a collaborative environment where experimental storytelling can thrive without the constraints often imposed by traditional network models. The series, still untitled, is reported to focus on a young woman navigating a world that is simultaneously intimate and alienating—a premise that dovetails with A24’s penchant for protagonists who are outsiders looking in.

Industry insiders speculate that the series could adopt a limited‑run format, perhaps eight to ten episodes, allowing Eisenberg to maintain tight narrative control while delivering a concise, impactful arc. Given his background in theatre and screenwriting, the project may also feature a strong emphasis on dialogue and character development, distinguishing it from the more plot‑driven fare that dominates much of contemporary streaming content. Moreover, Eisenberg’s involvement as director signals a visual style that could blend his theatrical sensibilities with A24’s signature cinematic flair—think atmospheric lighting, meticulous framing, and a willingness to linger on moments of quiet tension.

The partnership also underscores A24’s broader strategy of courting talent that straddles multiple disciplines. By aligning with creators like Eisenberg, the company continues to position itself as a haven for artists seeking creative freedom beyond the studio system. This approach has paid dividends, as A24’s recent ventures into television have garnered both critical praise and robust subscriber interest, reinforcing the label’s reputation as a tastemaker in the streaming era.

Looking ahead, the series could serve as a springboard for Eisenberg’s future projects, potentially opening doors to more ambitious television endeavors or even cross‑medium collaborations. As audiences increasingly gravitate toward content that offers depth and nuance, Eisenberg’s blend of literary wit and visual storytelling may resonate strongly with viewers craving fresh perspectives. While details about casting, release dates, and distribution platforms remain under wraps, the convergence of Eisenberg’s emerging directorial voice and A24’s curatorial expertise promises a compelling addition to the evolving landscape of prestige television.
